description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC NovaScribe reported a sudden spike of 5xx responses for embedding and streaming endpoints. Error rate climbed to ~18% for the tenant for ~40 minutes.
Impact: Customer-facing failures for real-time embedding and short chat responses; user-facing errors and degraded latency. Dedicated tenant on reserved pool; business impact medium-high.
Timeline: 09:08 - deploy of rate-limiter revamp to edge (canary 10%); 09:11 - Redis primary failover observed in us-east; 09:12 - customer alerts, 5xx spike begins; 09:50 - mitigation by rollback of rate-limiter canary; 10:05 - error rate returned to baseline.
Steps to reproduce: 1) On dedicated tenant with high short-lived connection churn, send 150 concurrent small embedding requests (1-2KB) over streaming endpoints; 2) Trigger simulated redis primary failover (failover script in staging); 3) Observe increased 502/503/504 from apigw and runtime restarts.
Observed logs: apigw: "upstream error: timeout connecting to rate-limiter"; rate-limiter: "redis: connection refused, entering degraded mode"; serving-runtime: "prefetch: evicting kV shards due to pool-thin"; autoscaler: "scaler: not enough healthy nodes for immediate backfill".
Immediate mitigation taken: Rolled back rate-limiter change at 09:50, temporarily increased apigw retry window, pinning tenant to warm prefetch policy, and opened emergency priority with infra (pager duty).
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Rate-limiter revamp introduced fallback path heavily dependent on Redis; during primary failover the fallback serialized requests causing apigw queue growth and runtime prefetch eviction.
Hypothesis 2: Dedicated pool thinning due to ephemeral node eviction + autoscaler slow backfill caused runtime OOMs and restarts amplifying 5xx.
Evidence: Redis failover events in logs (failover-id 20260310-09-11), slow redis reconnect latencies (500ms-2s), apigw accept queue increased to 12000, runtime memory churn correlated with 1.2s p50 latency spike.
Telemetry links: grafana/dashboards/tenant_novascribe/errors, logs/redis/us-east/failover-20260310
Next diagnostic steps: collect rate-limiter call traces, heap profiles from runtime around failure window, and full redis aof/replication lag snapshot.
comments: Support (Lena Kim) 2026-03-10 09:18 UTC: Customer reported 18% 5xx on embedding endpoints, providing request IDs and sample traces.
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-10 09:30 UTC: Correlated spike with redis failover events; investigating if new rate-limiter fallback path retries synchronously.
Customer (NovaScribe - Priya Rao) 2026-03-10 09:35 UTC: We saw failed requests in our logs; can you confirm if retrying will overwhelm systems?
SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-03-10 09:52 UTC: Rolled back rate-limiter canary; monitoring for recovery.
Support (Lena Kim) 2026-03-11 14:12 UTC: Follow-up: asking customer for postmortem access to logs; proposing a dedicated retry budget for this tenant.
resolution:
Mitigation: Rolled back rate-limiter change and applied a temporary retry budget to apigw for NovaScribe. Autoscaler policy adjusted to be more aggressive during failovers.
Root cause (tentative): Rate-limiter revamp introduced a synchronous fallback that relied on Redis; Redis primary failover caused cascading request serialization at the gateway which amplified runtime prefetch pressure and triggered transient restarts.
Permanent fix plan: 1) Implement async fallback with circuit-breaker and local in-memory token bucket; 2) Harden redis failover handling with shorter reconnect backoff and per-tenant isolation; 3) Add canary guardrails to detect Redis failover correlated spikes before wider rollout.
Follow-up owners: SRE (Diego Morales) for redis/backoff changes, Runtime team (Min-Jae Park) for prefetch isolation, Platform (Asha Patel) for canary guardrail implementation.
Status: Monitoring and scheduled follow-up rollout to staging on 2026-03-18.
